No NULL check after ucl_object_typed_new(UCL_STRING). If allocation fails and returns NULL, the next line dereferences the NULL pointer via obj->value.sv.

Changing < to <= in the delta balance check causes rotations when delta == -TREE_DELTA_MAX (i.e., -1), meaning the tree rotates on balanced subtrees. This corrupts the AVL tree structure during deep insertions, leading to a null pointer dereference when the rotation tries to access avl_right of a node that is NULL.

Replacing the height reset (= 0) with a no-op leaves the stale previous height value, so the max-child height computation compares against a garbage/stale value. This causes incorrect height values to propagate up the tree, breaking AVL balance invariants. Subsequent insertions can trigger rotations into uninitialized or already-freed subtree pointers, causing heap corruption.

A vulnerability exists in ucl_expand_variable where the expanded string buffer is allocated without space for the null terminator, causing a one-byte heap overflow.
